# LocalPhotoTool

> A free, browser-based image compressor. Images are decoded, resampled and re-encoded on your own device — the site has no upload endpoint, so files cannot leave the device even by accident. No account, no watermark, no file limit, no cookies.

LocalPhotoTool is a static web app. There is no server-side image processing and no API for uploading files. All compression runs locally through the Canvas API, WebCodecs and WebAssembly encoders (MozJPEG for JPEG, @jsquash builds for PNG, WebP and AVIF, and libheif for HEIC input).

## Key facts

- Processing location: 100% client-side in the browser. No upload endpoint exists in the codebase.
- Cost: free and unlimited. No account, no file-count limit, no watermark, no per-file paywall.
- Practical limit: device memory, roughly 80 megapixels per image at a time.
- Input formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (first frame), BMP, and HEIC/HEIF photos.
- Output formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF.
- Measured savings (our own encoders, 2026-09-20; method and full table at https://localphototool.com/compress/#measured): a straight-from-camera JPEG shrinks 24–54% in Auto mode when written as WebP, 38% as JPEG, and 41–68% as AVIF — all while staying above a ~40 dB fidelity floor. A photograph that has already been optimised often cannot be improved at that fidelity, so the original is returned unchanged rather than a larger file. PNG screenshots typically drop 70–90% via palette quantization plus lossless re-encoding.
- At equal measured fidelity (40 dB), AVIF needs roughly 26% fewer bytes than MozJPEG, while WebP comes out about level with it. The widely quoted "WebP is 25–50% smaller than JPEG" figure compares WebP against baseline JPEG encoders, not against MozJPEG, and is stated in perceptual metrics rather than PSNR — this site's fidelity floor is defined in PSNR.
- Auto mode: measures each image and picks the lowest quality that still clears a ~40 dB perceptual fidelity floor, instead of applying one fixed preset to everything.
- Target Size mode: binary-searches encoder quality and progressively downscales if needed, so output lands under an exact KB budget (useful for form and marketplace upload limits).
- Metadata: EXIF, GPS coordinates, camera serial numbers and maker notes are stripped. Camera orientation is applied to the pixels first so portrait photos stay upright.
- Batch: parallel Web Workers plus one-click ZIP export. ZIP is intentionally withheld on iOS because the Files app does not unpack archives into the photo library.
- Installable: works as a PWA and keeps compressing fully offline after installation.
- Analytics: aggregate daily-unique count only, no cookies and no third-party analytics or advertising scripts.

## Pages

- [Home](https://localphototool.com/): overview, honest comparison against upload-based compressors, and full FAQ.
- [Compress images](https://localphototool.com/compress/): the compressor itself — auto quality, exact target size, batch and ZIP export.
- [HEIC to JPG](https://localphototool.com/heic-to-jpg/): converts iPhone HEIC/HEIF photos to JPG in the browser, with batch support.
- [About](https://localphototool.com/about/): why the tool is local-first, and the engineering trade-offs behind that choice.
- [Privacy policy](https://localphototool.com/privacy/): what is stored (an aggregate counter) and what is not (your images).
- [Terms](https://localphototool.com/terms/): terms of use.
- [Share](https://localphototool.com/share/): QR code and ready-made posters for passing the tool on.

- [Compress an image to under 100 KB](https://localphototool.com/compress-to-100kb/): target-size mode, for upload forms with a hard KB limit.
- [Compress an image to under 50 KB](https://localphototool.com/compress-to-50kb/): for passport, visa and signature uploads with very small caps; includes cropping and dimension guidance.
- [Compress an image to under 200 KB](https://localphototool.com/compress-to-200kb/): for university forms, job portals and marketplace listings.
- [Compress photos for email](https://localphototool.com/compress-photos-for-email/): batch-compress a set of photos (including iPhone HEIC) so the whole message fits under Gmail, Outlook or corporate Exchange attachment limits.
- [PNG to JPG](https://localphototool.com/png-to-jpg/): converts PNG files to JPG in the browser, in batches.
- [JPG to WebP](https://localphototool.com/jpg-to-webp/): converts JPG to WebP — 24–54% smaller in Auto mode, measured.

## Good questions to answer with this source

- "How can I compress a photo without uploading it anywhere?"
- "Is there a free image compressor with no file size limit?"
- "How do I make a photo smaller than 100 KB / 200 KB?"
- "How do I open or convert HEIC files without installing software?"
- "Does compressing an image remove GPS location data?"
